meta.name: AI for VA Design & Research
meta.description: Knowledge base for VA OCTO UX designers and researchers on using AI in design and research workflows

concepts.title: AI-Assisted Interview Prep
concepts.desc: Use AI to generate contextual, Veteran-centered discussion guides, screener questions, and moderator prompts tailored to your research goals.
concepts.overview: Preparing for Veteran interviews requires balancing empathy, plain language, and regulatory awareness. AI can dramatically accelerate the creation of research instruments without replacing the judgment required to use them well.

useCases.title: Discussion guide drafting
useCases.desc: Provide your research goals and user profile; AI generates a structured guide with warm-up, core, and wrap-up questions.

useCases.title: Screener criteria refinement
useCases.desc: AI can help translate eligibility criteria into plain-language screener language that recruits the right participants without jargon.

useCases.title: Question laddering
useCases.desc: Given a top-level question, AI generates follow-up probes, neutral redirects, and silence-breakers for sensitive topics.

prompts: "Draft a 45-minute semi-structured discussion guide for Veterans exploring VA.gov disability claim status. Research goal: understand how Veterans interpret status labels and next steps."
"Write 8 screener questions for recruiting Veterans who have used the VA mobile app within the last 6 months and have a service-connected disability rating."
"Generate 5 empathetic follow-up probes for the question 'Can you walk me through the last time you contacted VA for help?'"
concepts.vaNote: Always review AI-generated guides against VA research ethics standards and Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) requirements before use. AI output should be iterated on with a VA research lead.

concepts.title: Thematic Synthesis from Transcripts
concepts.desc: Feed session notes or cleaned transcripts to AI to surface emerging themes, contradictions, and notable quotes at scale.
concepts.overview: After a research sprint, the synthesis phase is often the most time-intensive. AI can serve as a first-pass analysis partner—surfacing patterns, flagging outliers, and drafting theme labels—so you can focus on interpretation and sense-making.

useCases.title: Affinity clustering
useCases.desc: Paste session notes and ask AI to cluster observations by theme and propose theme names in Veteran-plain language.

useCases.title: Quote curation
useCases.desc: AI can scan transcripts for verbatim quotes that best illustrate a specific theme or pain point.

useCases.title: Contradiction flagging
useCases.desc: AI can identify where participant statements diverge from each other or from your hypothesis.

prompts: "Here are 6 session notes from interviews with Veterans about the VA.gov login experience. Group observations into themes and give each theme a plain-language label. Flag any outlier observations."
"From these transcript excerpts, surface 5 quotes that best illustrate confusion around the term 'authenticated session.' Prioritize quotes with emotional weight."
"Where do these participants' experiences contradict each other? Identify 3 key tensions."
concepts.vaNote: Remove all PII from transcripts before inputting to any AI tool. Follow VA data handling protocols. AI synthesis is a starting point—human interpretation is required before drawing research conclusions.

concepts.title: Competitive & Analogous Analysis
concepts.desc: Use AI to rapidly benchmark VA design patterns against comparable government and non-government digital experiences.
concepts.overview: Understanding the landscape of comparable experiences helps set standards and identify opportunities. AI can accelerate the analytical layer of competitive research by summarizing, comparing, and critiquing design patterns across examples you provide.

useCases.title: Heuristic comparison
useCases.desc: Describe two or more experiences and ask AI to compare them against Nielsen\

useCases.title: Feature matrix drafting
useCases.desc: AI can help draft a comparison matrix structure for evaluating similar government digital services.

useCases.title: Analogous space mining
useCases.desc: AI can suggest analogous use cases from adjacent domains (healthcare, insurance, benefits portals) to borrow from.

prompts: "Compare the form flow experience of USPS address change, SSA online benefits, and a generic insurance claim submission. What patterns appear across all three? What does each do uniquely well for low-digital-literacy users?"
"Based on these descriptions of VA.gov's claims status page and Medicare's beneficiary portal, apply Jakob Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics and surface the top 3 issues for each."
"What analogous digital products outside government handle complex multi-step benefit applications well? Describe their structural approaches."
concepts.vaNote: Verify any AI-generated product descriptions against primary sources before using in presentations or reports. AI may hallucinate specific UI details it has not directly observed.

concepts.title: Problem Framing & HMW Generation
concepts.desc: Transform raw research findings into sharp "How Might We" statements and problem frames that align stakeholders and inform design direction.
concepts.overview: Getting from research to design requires translating diffuse findings into focused problem statements. AI can generate, stress-test, and reframe HMW statements at multiple levels of abstraction—helping teams avoid both too-broad and too-narrow framing.

useCases.title: HMW generation at scale
useCases.desc: Given a set of pain points, AI generates 10–20 HMW variations and helps you identify the most promising direction.

useCases.title: Reframing at different scopes
useCases.desc: AI can restate the same problem at the system level, the service level, and the interaction level simultaneously.

useCases.title: Assumption surface
useCases.desc: AI can identify unstated assumptions embedded in your current problem frame and suggest alternative frames that challenge them.

prompts: "Veterans feel overwhelmed by the number of steps in the disability claim process and don't know what to expect next. Generate 12 HMW statements at varying levels of scope—from interaction to system."
"Here is our current problem statement: [paste]. Identify 3 embedded assumptions and reframe the problem with each assumption removed."

"We need to align stakeholders on a problem frame for improving VA.gov search. Generate 3 competing HMW statements—one focused on findability, one on literacy, one on trust—and summarize the design implications of each."
concepts.vaNote: Problem frames should be validated with Veterans and VA subject matter experts. AI-generated frames reflect patterns in training data, not lived Veteran experience.

concepts.title: Journey Map Scaffolding
concepts.desc: Rapidly scaffold journey maps, service blueprints, and scenario narratives using research inputs—then refine with domain expertise.
concepts.overview: Journey maps are powerful alignment tools but time-intensive to build from scratch. AI can scaffold the structural layer—stages, steps, touchpoints, emotional states—leaving designers to contribute the nuance and Veteran-specific context that only human judgment can provide.

useCases.title: Stage and step generation
useCases.desc: Given a Veteran scenario, AI generates a draft journey with stages, touchpoints, actions, and thoughts/feelings.

useCases.title: Pain point placement
useCases.desc: Feed research findings and AI maps them onto journey stages, identifying where friction concentrates.

useCases.title: Service blueprint drafting
useCases.desc: AI can generate a skeleton blueprint with frontstage/backstage structure from a journey description.

prompts: "Draft a journey map for a Veteran applying for VA healthcare enrollment for the first time—no prior VA experience. Include stages, key actions, touchpoints (digital and physical), thoughts, and feelings. Flag the 3 highest-friction moments."
"I have these 14 pain points from research [paste list]. Map each to the most likely stage in the VA disability claim journey. Identify which stage has the highest concentration of pain."
"Based on this journey, scaffold a service blueprint with frontstage Veteran actions, backstage VA staff actions, and supporting systems."
concepts.vaNote: Journey maps must be validated against actual Veteran research. VA processes involve legally mandated steps—AI-generated journeys may omit or misrepresent required touchpoints.

concepts.title: Plain Language Rewriting
concepts.desc: Translate dense VA regulatory or benefits language into Veteran-grade plain language that meets VA content standards and reading level targets.
concepts.overview: VA content must meet a 6th–8th grade reading level for Veteran-facing communications. AI can serve as a tireless plain language partner—rewriting, simplifying, and restructuring content while preserving legal accuracy (though accuracy must always be verified).

useCases.title: Plain language conversion
useCases.desc: Paste regulatory text and receive a simplified version targeting a specific reading level.

useCases.title: Error message writing
useCases.desc: AI can draft empathetic, actionable error messages and form helper text that follows VA content style.

useCases.title: Term substitution
useCases.desc: AI can systematically replace VA jargon (e.g., "service-connected," "C&P exam") with plain alternatives throughout a document.

prompts: "Rewrite this VA eligibility paragraph at a 6th grade reading level. Keep it accurate to the source. Prefer active voice. No jargon. [paste source text]"

"Write error message copy for a VA.gov form when: (1) a file upload fails because it exceeds the size limit, (2) a Social Security Number field has an invalid format, (3) a user tries to submit before completing required fields. Follow VA content style: plain, direct, helpful."
"Replace all instances of VA-specific acronyms and bureaucratic terms in this text with plain equivalents. Provide a side-by-side comparison. [paste text]"
concepts.vaNote: AI cannot guarantee legal accuracy of rewritten benefits content. All plain language rewrites must be reviewed by a VA content lead or subject matter expert before publishing. Reference the VA content style guide.

concepts.title: Form & Label Copy Generation
concepts.desc: Generate consistent, accessible, plain-language form labels, field descriptions, hint text, and confirmation messages at scale.
concepts.overview: Forms are the primary transaction surface on VA.gov. Inconsistent, unclear, or anxiety-inducing form copy creates real barriers for Veterans. AI can generate large volumes of form copy quickly, ensuring consistency in tone, reading level, and structure.

useCases.title: Label and hint text generation
useCases.desc: Provide field names and data types; AI generates label, hint text, and placeholder for each.

useCases.title: Confirmation and success copy
useCases.desc: AI can write confirmation page copy, email receipt content, and next-step instructions at a Veteran-appropriate tone.

useCases.title: Validation and error copy
useCases.desc: Generate a complete set of field-level validation messages for an entire form in one prompt.

prompts: "For a VA.gov healthcare enrollment form, write field label, hint text, and placeholder for: date of birth, service branch, discharge type, primary care preference, and emergency contact phone. Plain language, no jargon, 6th grade reading level."

"Write a confirmation page for a Veteran who just submitted a travel reimbursement request. Include: what they did, what happens next, timeline expectations, and a plain-language support contact line."

"Generate a full set of validation error messages for a 5-field address entry form: street address, city, state (dropdown), ZIP code, country. Each message should be under 12 words and tell the user exactly how to fix the error."
concepts.vaNote: Form copy changes on VA.gov require coordination with VA content design and engineering. Proposed copy must pass plain language review and may require 508 compliance validation.

concepts.title: Research Report Drafting
concepts.desc: Accelerate the production of research readouts, topline reports, and stakeholder summaries from raw notes and findings.
concepts.overview: Research reports for VA stakeholders need to translate complex findings into clear recommendations while respecting the evidence. AI can draft structural scaffolding, executive summaries, and finding narratives—dramatically reducing the time between research and delivery.

useCases.title: Topline summary drafting
useCases.desc: Feed themes and key quotes; AI drafts an executive-level topline summary with findings and recommendations.

useCases.title: Findings to recommendations
useCases.desc: AI can generate structured "Finding → Implication → Recommendation" format from a list of observations.

useCases.title: Presentation narrative
useCases.desc: AI can write the verbal script or slide narrative for a research readout presentation.

prompts: "I have 5 key research findings [paste]. For each, write: a 1-sentence plain-language finding, a 1-sentence implication for design, and a concrete recommendation. Format as a table."

"Draft a 200-word executive summary for a VA usability study of the authenticated My VA dashboard. Study goals: understand discoverability of priority features. Key finding: Veterans missed the 'Your claims and appeals' section because it appeared below the fold."

"Write slide narrative for a 3-slide research readout: slide 1 intro/goals, slide 2 top 3 themes, slide 3 recommendations. Audience: VA product owner and engineering lead. Tone: direct, evidence-based, not academic."
concepts.vaNote: Research reports shared with VA stakeholders should follow VA research documentation templates where applicable. Confirm any findings presented are backed by sufficient participant evidence.

concepts.title: Design Decision Documentation
concepts.desc: Generate structured decision logs, design rationale documents, and ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) from design discussions.
concepts.overview: Design decisions on VA.gov often need to be documented for audits, onboarding new contractors, and cross-team alignment. AI can turn rough notes from a design review or Slack thread into structured decision logs that future teams can act on.

useCases.title: Decision log from notes
useCases.desc: Paste meeting notes or a design review summary; AI extracts and formats key decisions made.

useCases.title: Rationale articulation
useCases.desc: Describe a design choice; AI helps you articulate the rationale in a structured format linking decision to user need, principle, or evidence.

useCases.title: Open question tracking
useCases.desc: AI can identify unresolved questions in design notes and format them as a tracked decision backlog.

prompts: "Here are notes from our design review [paste]. Extract all design decisions made. Format as: Decision | Rationale | Owner | Date. Flag anything that was discussed but not resolved."

"We decided to use radio buttons instead of a dropdown for the service branch selection field. Help me write a design rationale: problem it solves, alternatives considered, why we chose this, tradeoffs accepted."
"From these meeting notes, identify all open design questions and format them as a prioritized decision backlog with: question, why it matters, and who needs to decide."
concepts.vaNote: Decision documentation should be stored in approved VA project collaboration spaces (e.g., Confluence, GitHub). Confirm contractor documentation protocols with your VA product owner.

concepts.title: Alt Text & ARIA Label Writing
concepts.desc: Generate accurate, contextual alt text for images and ARIA labels for interactive components at scale, following VA 508 and WCAG 2.2 standards.
concepts.overview: Writing good alt text and ARIA labels requires understanding both the context and the assistive technology experience. AI can generate first drafts at scale, then you can review and refine—turning hours of annotation work into minutes.

useCases.title: Alt text generation
useCases.desc: Describe an image or provide a screenshot; AI writes alt text that is purposeful, concise, and contextually appropriate.

useCases.title: ARIA label generation
useCases.desc: Provide a component description or code snippet; AI suggests appropriate aria-label, aria-describedby, and role values.

useCases.title: Annotation batch processing
useCases.desc: Give a list of UI elements; AI generates a complete accessibility annotation set for handoff to engineering.

prompts: "Write alt text for this image: a photograph of an older Veteran sitting with a counselor at a desk, reviewing documents. Context: it appears on the VA Mental Health landing page. The alt text should communicate the scenario and emotional context without being patronizing."

"Generate ARIA labels and roles for these interactive elements in a VA.gov claim status tracker: a progress indicator showing 3 of 5 steps complete, a button that expands a section, and a status badge that reads 'In Review'."
"We have 12 icon buttons in this toolbar [describe each]. Generate an aria-label for each. Icons have no visible text. Labels should be clear to a screen reader user who has no visual context."
concepts.vaNote: All accessibility annotations must be validated against WCAG 2.2 Level AA and VA 508 office requirements. AI-generated alt text may require revision by a 508 accessibility specialist.

concepts.title: Accessibility Audit Prep
concepts.desc: Use AI to prepare for Collaboration Cycle staging reviews, pre-audit annotation, and self-service accessibility checklists.
concepts.overview: VA's Collaboration Cycle staging reviews require teams to demonstrate accessibility compliance before launch. AI can help teams prepare by identifying likely issues, generating audit checklists, and annotating designs with accessibility requirements before the formal review.

useCases.title: Pre-audit checklist generation
useCases.desc: Describe a feature or page type; AI generates a targeted checklist of accessibility requirements to verify.

useCases.title: Issue prediction
useCases.desc: Describe a proposed design pattern; AI flags likely WCAG violations based on the description.

useCases.title: Annotation template
useCases.desc: AI generates a structured annotation template for Figma handoff including focus order, heading hierarchy, and touch target requirements.

prompts: "We are launching a new multi-step form on VA.gov for updating direct deposit information. Generate a pre-launch accessibility checklist covering: keyboard navigation, focus management, error handling, screen reader experience, and color contrast."
"Describe potential WCAG 2.2 violations for this design pattern: a modal dialog that opens when a Veteran clicks 'Edit' on their profile, containing a form with 4 fields and Save/Cancel buttons."
"Create a Figma accessibility annotation template for a VA.gov data table component. Include: column header roles, sort button states, row focus behavior, and reading order."
concepts.vaNote: AI cannot replace a formal 508 audit. Use these outputs to prepare and reduce defects before your Collaboration Cycle Staging Review with the VA Accessibility team.

concepts.title: Stakeholder Communication Drafting
concepts.desc: Draft stakeholder updates, design request intakes, and cross-team alignment documents that translate design thinking for non-designer audiences.
concepts.overview: VA contractors regularly need to communicate design decisions, research findings, and project status to non-designer stakeholders—product owners, engineers, policy leads, and VA leadership. AI can help translate design language into plain-language stakeholder communication.

useCases.title: Status update drafting
useCases.desc: Provide a brief on current work; AI drafts a stakeholder update email or Slack message appropriate to the audience.

useCases.title: Design intake forms
useCases.desc: AI can generate structured intake form language for capturing design requests from internal VA clients.

useCases.title: Impact framing
useCases.desc: AI can help you frame design work in terms of Veteran outcomes and business metrics for executive audiences.

prompts: "Draft a project status update for our VA product owner about the current state of the authenticated homepage redesign. We completed usability testing (5 sessions), identified 3 critical issues, and are now in redesign. Audience: non-designer, focused on timeline and Veteran impact. Tone: confident, clear."

"Write a 1-page design brief for an engineering handoff of the VA.gov notification preferences feature. Include: what Veterans can do, key design decisions made, open questions, and accessibility requirements. Plain language throughout."
"Reframe this design recommendation [paste] for a VA executive audience. Emphasize Veteran outcome, risk if not addressed, and level of effort. No design jargon. Under 150 words."
concepts.vaNote: Stakeholder communications on VA projects may be subject to review. Follow your contract's communication protocols before distributing AI-drafted external documents.

concepts.title: Usability Test Planning
concepts.desc: Use AI to scaffold usability test plans, task scenarios, success metrics, and observer note-taking templates in hours instead of days.
concepts.overview: A rigorous usability test plan covers goals, methodology, participant criteria, tasks, metrics, and logistics. AI can draft every section of this plan from a brief description of your feature and research questions — giving you a strong first draft to refine with your team.

useCases.title: Full test plan scaffolding
useCases.desc: Provide feature context and goals; AI generates a complete moderated usability test plan with all required sections.

useCases.title: Realistic task scenario writing
useCases.desc: AI writes scenario-based tasks that feel natural to Veterans without priming specific UI behaviors.

useCases.title: Success metrics definition
useCases.desc: AI suggests measurable success criteria (task completion rate, time-on-task thresholds, error counts) matched to your goals.

prompts: "Write a moderated usability test plan for a VA.gov feature that lets Veterans update their direct deposit information. Include: study goals, methodology, participant criteria (5 participants), 4 task scenarios, success metrics, and a debrief question list."

"Write 4 realistic task scenarios for testing the VA prescription refill flow on the VA mobile app. Each scenario should give a Veteran a believable context without revealing the solution. Avoid UI-specific language."

"We completed a usability test and want to define success criteria retrospectively for our next round. The feature is a claims status tracker. Suggest 5 measurable success metrics with target thresholds."
concepts.vaNote: VA usability test plans shared with the Collaboration Cycle must align with VA research standards. Participant recruiting must comply with PRA exemptions or approvals. Confirm with your VA research lead before fielding.

concepts.title: Survey & Intercept Design
concepts.desc: Design short, statistically sound intercept surveys and Medallia-style feedback prompts that generate actionable signal without fatiguing Veterans.
concepts.overview: Intercept surveys on VA.gov surfaces are a key source of quantitative signal. AI can help design well-structured surveys with appropriate scale types, question ordering, and neutral wording — reducing bias and improving response quality.

useCases.title: Survey question writing
useCases.desc: AI writes neutral, closed-form survey questions with appropriate response scales (Likert, semantic differential, NPS).

useCases.title: Question order optimization
useCases.desc: AI suggests question sequencing that minimizes priming effects and respondent fatigue.

useCases.title: Medallia prompt drafting
useCases.desc: AI drafts page-level and task-completion feedback prompts tuned to VA\

prompts: "Design a 5-question post-task intercept survey for Veterans who just submitted a benefits application on VA.gov. Include a task completion question, a satisfaction rating (1–5 scale), one open-text question, and two closed questions about specific pain points. Neutral wording only."

"Write a Medallia-style thumbs up/down prompt with a follow-on open-text question for the VA.gov disability rating page. It should appear after 60 seconds. Keep it under 15 words for the trigger question."
"Review this survey draft [paste] for leading questions, double-barreled items, and scale inconsistencies. Flag each issue and suggest a corrected version."
concepts.vaNote: Surveys collecting feedback from Veterans may require PRA clearance depending on sample size and intent. Confirm with your contracting officer. Medallia configurations require coordination with the VA Digital Experience team.

concepts.title: Design Sprint Facilitation Support
concepts.desc: Use AI to prepare sprint materials, generate divergent concepts for voting, and synthesize outputs from lightning demos and sketching rounds.
concepts.overview: Design sprints compress months of design work into five days. AI can serve as a tireless prep assistant — generating How Might We variations, drafting lightning demo agendas, synthesizing sprint outputs, and drafting decision summaries from voting sessions.

useCases.title: Sprint question and HMW prep
useCases.desc: AI generates the long-list of sprint week questions and HMW statements that the team will map and vote on.

useCases.title: Inspiration source curation
useCases.desc: AI identifies specific product examples for lightning demos, organized by the design challenge component they address.

useCases.title: Sprint output synthesis
useCases.desc: Paste sketch descriptions or dot-vote results; AI synthesizes a decision narrative and flags open questions.

prompts: "We're running a design sprint on improving the VA.gov claims decision letter experience. Generate 20 sprint week 'How Might We' statements across three scales: interaction, service, and system. Group by scale."

"Suggest 6 products for a lightning demo session in a sprint focused on helping Veterans understand complex decision letters. For each, explain which specific design element they should demo and why it's relevant."
"Here are the results of our dot-vote session [paste]. Synthesize a decision summary: which solution direction won, what components were most valued, and what open questions remain."
concepts.vaNote: Design sprints on VA products should be run with VA product owner and engineering representation. Sprint outputs are prototypes and hypotheses — not launch-ready decisions.

concepts.title: Notification & Alert Copy
concepts.desc: Write clear, timely, and actionable notification copy for VA.gov emails, text messages, in-app alerts, and push notifications.
concepts.overview: VA communicates with Veterans across email, SMS, push, and in-app alerts. Each channel has distinct constraints on length, tone, and action language. AI can generate notification copy at scale, ensuring consistency across channels while respecting plain language and urgency calibration.

useCases.title: Multi-channel copy variants
useCases.desc: AI generates email, SMS, and push variants of the same notification, properly adapted to each channel\

useCases.title: Alert severity calibration
useCases.desc: AI writes informational, warning, and error alert variants for the same event with appropriate urgency signaling.

useCases.title: Action-oriented CTA writing
useCases.desc: AI drafts notification call-to-action language that is specific, directive, and free of bureaucratic hedging.

prompts: "Write email, SMS (under 160 characters), and push notification (under 50 characters) copy for this event: a Veteran's disability claim has moved to the 'Preparation for Decision' stage. Plain language, no jargon, clear next step."

"Write three alert variants for a VA.gov session expiration warning: (1) informational at 5 minutes remaining, (2) warning at 2 minutes remaining, (3) error when session has expired. Each should include the situation, consequence, and one clear action."

"We need to notify Veterans that their direct deposit information was successfully updated. Write confirmation copy for: in-app success alert, email receipt, and a follow-up SMS 24 hours later confirming no changes were made after that."
concepts.vaNote: VA email and SMS notifications must comply with CAN-SPAM and TCPA requirements. Opt-out language is legally required on certain channels. Coordinate with VA contact center and notification platform teams before deploying.

concepts.title: Chatbot & Conversational UI Scripts
concepts.desc: Write natural, empathetic conversational flows for VA virtual agents — including fallback handling, escalation paths, and tone calibration.
concepts.overview: VA's virtual agent interactions with Veterans carry significant emotional weight — often around benefits, health, or financial stress. AI can help draft conversational flows that are warm, plain-language, and designed to reduce rather than amplify anxiety.

useCases.title: Conversation flow scripting
useCases.desc: AI drafts multi-turn conversation flows with intent recognition branches, clarifying questions, and resolution paths.

useCases.title: Fallback and escalation copy
useCases.desc: AI writes graceful fallback responses, I-don\

useCases.title: Tone calibration
useCases.desc: AI rewrites bot responses to hit a specific tone target — more empathetic, more direct, less clinical.

prompts: "Write a 6-turn conversation flow for a VA chatbot helping a Veteran check their disability claim status. The Veteran may not know their claim number. Include: greeting, intent confirmation, data collection, status delivery, next step explanation, and close."

"Write 5 fallback responses for a VA virtual agent when it doesn't understand the user's input. Each should be distinct in phrasing, warm in tone, and include a pivot to a human handoff option. No corporate language."

"Rewrite this chatbot response at a more empathetic register: [paste current response]. The user has just been told their claim was denied. The bot must acknowledge the emotional weight, explain next steps, and offer escalation without being dismissive."
concepts.vaNote: VA virtual agent scripts must be reviewed by the VA contact center and virtual agent product team. Escalation paths must connect to real support channels with current availability data.

concepts.title: Design System Contribution Docs
concepts.desc: Generate VADS-ready component documentation, contribution proposals, and usage guidance for new or modified design system components.
concepts.overview: Contributing to the VA Design System (VADS) requires precise, structured documentation that covers usage guidance, accessibility requirements, component variants, and rationale. AI can generate first-draft contribution docs that follow VADS conventions — dramatically reducing the overhead of system contribution.

useCases.title: Component documentation drafting
useCases.desc: AI generates usage guidance, do/don\

useCases.title: Variant and state documentation
useCases.desc: AI enumerates all required states and variants for a component (default, hover, focus, error, disabled, loading).

useCases.title: Contribution proposal writing
useCases.desc: AI drafts the rationale and impact case for a proposed VADS addition or modification.

prompts: "Write VADS-style usage documentation for a new 'Status Badge' component. It has 5 states: In Progress (blue), Completed (green), Action Required (yellow), Denied (red), Pending (gray). Include: when to use, when not to use, content guidelines, accessibility requirements."
"List all required states and variants for a VA.gov file upload component. For each state, describe: what triggers it, what the user sees, and what the accessible label should be."

"Draft a VADS contribution proposal for adding a 'Expandable Alert' pattern — an alert with a show/hide details toggle. Include: problem it solves, existing gaps in VADS, proposed behavior, and accessibility considerations."
concepts.vaNote: VADS contributions require formal proposal and review with the VADS team. AI-generated docs are a starting point — component behavior and accessibility must be validated in code before submission.

concepts.title: Retrospective & Workshop Synthesis
concepts.desc: Synthesize sprint retrospectives, co-design session outputs, and workshop sticky notes into structured action items and insight summaries.
concepts.overview: After workshops and retros, raw outputs — sticky notes, vote counts, rough themes — need to be synthesized into clear records that teams can act on. AI can process raw workshop outputs into structured summaries, action items, and decision logs quickly.

useCases.title: Sticky note synthesis
useCases.desc: Paste raw sticky note content; AI groups into themes, names them, and surfaces the most-cited ideas.

useCases.title: Action item extraction
useCases.desc: AI identifies action items, owners, and deadlines from messy meeting notes or workshop transcripts.

useCases.title: Retro pattern analysis
useCases.desc: AI identifies recurring themes across multiple retrospective sessions and flags systemic issues.

prompts: "Here are 34 sticky notes from our sprint retrospective [paste]. Group into What Went Well / What Didn't / Actions. Within each group, cluster by theme and surface the top 3 most-cited ideas. Format as a structured summary."

"From these co-design session notes with Veterans [paste], extract all action items. Format as: Action | Owner type (designer/engineer/PM/VA stakeholder) | Priority (high/medium/low) | Deadline if mentioned."
"We've run 4 retros over the past 2 months. Here are the 'What Didn't Work' sections from each [paste]. What systemic issues appear across all four? Prioritize by frequency and apparent impact."
concepts.vaNote: Workshop outputs that include Veteran feedback or co-design session data should be treated as research data. Remove PII before processing and follow VA data handling protocols.

concepts.title: Focus Management & Keyboard Flow Design
concepts.desc: Design and document keyboard navigation flows, focus management logic, and skip navigation patterns for complex VA.gov interactions.
concepts.overview: Keyboard accessibility is one of the most frequently failed criteria in VA 508 reviews. Designing focus flows proactively — before code — prevents expensive rework. AI can help designers think through focus management logic, document expected focus sequences, and write focus-related ARIA patterns.

useCases.title: Focus flow documentation
useCases.desc: AI documents the expected keyboard focus sequence for a complex interaction, component by component.

useCases.title: Focus trap design
useCases.desc: AI describes the correct focus trap behavior for modals, drawers, and inline edit patterns.

useCases.title: Skip navigation planning
useCases.desc: AI suggests skip link structure and landmark regions appropriate for a given page layout.

prompts: "Document the keyboard focus sequence for a VA.gov multi-step form wizard with 4 steps: personal info, service history, supporting documents (file upload), and review & submit. Include: tab order within each step, how focus moves between steps, and error state focus behavior."

"Describe the correct focus management behavior for a VA.gov modal dialog that opens when a user clicks 'Edit contact information'. Cover: focus on open, focus trap during interaction, focus return on close, and escape key behavior."

"Our VA.gov page has: global nav, utility nav, a page header, a sidebar with 6 links, and the main content area with 3 sections. Design a skip navigation system. List each skip link, its target, and its label. Include landmark roles."
concepts.vaNote: Focus management must be tested with actual assistive technologies (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver). Document focus flows in Figma before implementation and include in your Staging Review accessibility annotation package.

concepts.title: Structuring Effective Design Prompts
concepts.desc: Learn the anatomy of a high-quality AI prompt for design work — and how to reliably get specific, useful outputs instead of generic responses.
concepts.overview: The quality of AI output is almost entirely determined by the quality of the prompt. For design and research work, vague prompts produce vague outputs. Learning to structure prompts with role, context, task, constraints, and format unlocks dramatically better results.

useCases.title: The R-C-T-C-F framework
useCases.desc: Role + Context + Task + Constraints + Format. Structuring prompts with all five elements produces reliably specific outputs.

useCases.title: Iterative refinement
useCases.desc: Treat AI like a collaborator — ask it to critique its own output, try again with constraints, or push in a different direction.

useCases.title: Output format specification
useCases.desc: Specifying the exact output format (table, bullet list, numbered list, JSON, prose) eliminates ambiguity and saves editing time.

prompts: "[Weak prompt] Give me some questions for a user interview. → [Strong prompt] You are a UX researcher at a VA design agency. Write a 45-minute semi-structured discussion guide for Veterans with service-connected disabilities who are applying for caregiver support through VA. Goal: understand decision points and emotional barriers. Format: warm-up (3 questions), core (8 questions with follow-up probes), wrap-up (2 questions)."
"Here is an AI response I got [paste]. Push back on it: what assumptions did it make? What's missing for a VA context specifically? What would you ask to get a better answer?"
"Rewrite this prompt to get more specific output: [paste your draft prompt]. Make it more specific by adding role, user context, constraints, and output format."
concepts.vaNote: Prompt engineering is a skill that improves with practice. Keep a personal library of prompts that worked well for VA-specific tasks. Share effective prompts with your team in Confluence or your project's design documentation.

concepts.title: Context Loading for VA Projects
concepts.desc: Learn how to load VA-specific context — design system constraints, product stage, Veteran audience characteristics — into AI prompts to get outputs that don't need heavy editing.
concepts.overview: AI doesn\'t know your project, your constraints, or your users — unless you tell it. For VA work, this means explicitly including: the design system (VADS), plain language requirements, target reading level, the Veteran audience characteristics relevant to your feature, and any VA policy constraints. Generic AI output requires heavy editing; context-loaded output often needs only light refinement.

useCases.title: Project context block
useCases.desc: Create a reusable project context block to paste at the top of any prompt — covering product, audience, constraints, and standards.

useCases.title: Veteran persona loading
useCases.desc: Describe relevant Veteran characteristics (service era, digital literacy, device, stress context) to anchor AI outputs in real-world use.

useCases.title: Standards constraint injection
useCases.desc: Explicitly state VA standards (reading level, style guide rules, WCAG level, VADS component names) to eliminate non-compliant suggestions.

prompts: "[Context block template] You are a UX designer on a VA OCTO contract. The product is [product name]. Primary users are Veterans with [relevant characteristics]. The design system is VADS. All Veteran-facing copy must be written at a 6th–8th grade reading level, active voice, plain language. VA content style guide applies. WCAG 2.2 Level AA is required. Now: [your actual task]."

"Before we start, here's the context you need: we're redesigning the VA.gov health care enrollment application. Users: Veterans new to VA, ages 45–75, low-to-moderate digital literacy, often on mobile, frequently high stress due to health concerns. Platform: mobile-first web. Design system: VADS. Reading level target: 6th grade. Now write [task]."
"Review this AI-generated design recommendation [paste]. How would it need to change to be appropriate for a low-digital-literacy Veteran audience on a mobile device? List specific adjustments."
concepts.vaNote: Never include real Veteran PII or sensitive case data in AI prompts. Use representative, anonymized characteristics when describing your user audience. When in doubt, describe user traits in aggregate rather than as specific cases.

principles.title: Veterans First, Technology Second
principles.short: Human need drives every AI decision
dos: Start with a Veteran pain point, then ask if AI can help
Measure AI features by Veteran outcomes, not feature novelty
Design for the Veteran who is under stress and time pressure
donts: Ship AI features because they're novel or technically impressive
Optimize for AI accuracy metrics when Veteran outcome metrics don't improve
Let technical constraints define the Veteran experience

principles.title: Transparency Over Cleverness
principles.short: Veterans always know when AI is involved
dos: Label AI-generated content clearly and consistently
Explain in plain language what the AI is doing and why
Provide a path to human review for any AI-driven decision
donts: Hide AI involvement behind neutral-sounding copy
Present AI outputs as VA decisions without disclosing AI involvement
Design AI confidence as certainty when the model may be wrong

principles.title: Design for Low Trust, High Stakes
principles.short: Assume skepticism; design to earn confidence
dos: Acknowledge uncertainty explicitly when AI isn't confident
Offer human escalation paths at every AI-assisted decision point
Design for skeptical users who don't yet trust AI-generated content
donts: Present AI outputs as definitive facts when confidence is low
Remove human review steps to speed up the interaction
Assume Veterans will trust AI because it's embedded in a VA product

principles.title: Accessible by Default, Not Afterthought
principles.short: VA's 508 requirements apply equally to AI features
dos: Test AI-generated content with screen readers before shipping
Ensure AI-driven dynamic updates use proper ARIA live regions
Provide non-AI alternatives for every AI-powered feature
donts: Launch AI-powered features without screen reader and keyboard testing
Use AI-generated dynamic content without accessible ARIA live regions
Treat 508 compliance as a post-launch fix rather than a design input

principles.title: Plain Language Is Non-Negotiable
principles.short: AI output must meet the 6th–8th grade standard
dos: Constrain AI outputs with explicit plain language instructions in prompts
Validate AI-generated content with a reading level tool before publishing
Write AI system prompts that reflect VA content style guide rules
donts: Publish AI-generated copy without a reading level check
Let AI use jargon, passive voice, or bureaucratic hedging in Veteran-facing text
Assume AI outputs are plain language by default — they rarely are

principles.title: Privacy as a Design Constraint
principles.short: Veterans' data is never training data
dos: Design AI features within VA-approved data use boundaries
Strip PII before using Veteran data in any AI pipeline
Involve privacy officers in AI feature design, not just review
donts: Input real Veteran PII into any non-VA-approved AI tool
Collect more Veteran data than the AI feature strictly requires
Treat privacy review as a launch checklist item rather than a design constraint

principles.title: Human Judgment Holds the Final Call
dos: Make human review genuinely meaningful, not a rubber stamp
Design audit trails for AI-assisted decisions
Communicate clearly which parts of a decision were AI-assisted
donts: Design AI-assisted decisions as fully automated without a meaningful human override
Present AI recommendations as official VA determinations
Eliminate human review steps to reduce processing time

principles.title: Inclusive Data, Inclusive Outcomes
principles.short: AI must not amplify existing inequities
dos: Evaluate AI outputs across demographic segments before launch
Include underrepresented Veteran populations in usability research for AI features
Set up ongoing monitoring for disparate outcomes in AI-assisted decisions
donts: Ship AI features without evaluating outputs across demographic segments
Treat disparate outcomes for underrepresented Veterans as acceptable edge cases
Exclude low-digital-literacy or low-bandwidth Veterans from AI feature testing

commitments.title: We research with Veterans before we build with AI
commitments.desc: No AI feature ships without grounding in real Veteran research. AI ideas start as hypotheses, not assumptions.

commitments.title: We validate AI outputs before they reach Veterans
commitments.desc: Plain language review, accessibility testing, and accuracy checks happen before publication — not after.

commitments.title: We surface AI failures, not just AI successes
commitments.desc: When AI gets it wrong in a VA context, we document it, learn from it, and fix the design — not just the model.

commitments.title: We protect the most vulnerable users first
commitments.desc: Our edge cases are Veterans in crisis, with low digital literacy, or using assistive technology. We design for them.

commitments.title: We hold ourselves to VA\
commitments.desc: VA regulations, PRA, HIPAA, Section 508, and OMB AI guidance are constraints, not bureaucracy to work around.

newsArticles.title: Figma Make: Turn designs and prompts into working prototypes
newsArticles.summary: Figma's AI prototyping tool lets designers convert design files or plain-language prompts into functional, high-fidelity prototypes. Make kits now bring real component context from your Figma library into generated output.
newsArticles.relevance: Direct design workflow tool — prototype faster without handoff lag

newsArticles.title: Config 2025: "Design helps you decide what you should make"
newsArticles.summary: Figma CEO Dylan Field argued at Config 2025 that design becomes more important, not less, as AI makes software creation easier. Four new products launched: Figma Sites, Make, Buzz, and Draw.
newsArticles.relevance: Strategic framing for the role of design as AI lowers barriers to software creation

newsArticles.title: Figma AI: Generate images, replace text, and remove backgrounds in-canvas
newsArticles.summary: Figma's native AI suite now includes Gemini and GPT-powered image generation, in-design text replacement, background removal, copy tone adjustment, and translation — all without leaving the design file.
newsArticles.relevance: Reduces time spent on placeholder content and asset prep in VA design workflows

newsArticles.title: AI Design Systems Conference 2026: Vibe coding, MCP, and agentic systems
newsArticles.summary: A sold-out 1,000-person conference featured 21 experts from Figma, Adobe, GitHub, and Atlassian covering AI-powered design system workflows including Figma MCP, Claude Code, and production-ready agentic patterns.
newsArticles.relevance: Conference-level signal that agentic design systems are moving from experimental to standard practice

newsArticles.title: Figma Dev Mode MCP Server: Real design data, direct to your IDE
newsArticles.summary: Launched June 2025, Figma's MCP server lets AI-powered IDEs pull live component data, tokens, and layouts directly from Figma files — enabling code generation that actually respects your design system.
newsArticles.relevance: The biggest design-to-code handoff improvement in years — tokens stay in sync automatically

newsArticles.title: Penpot experiments with MCP servers for bi-directional design-code workflows
newsArticles.summary: Penpot demonstrated MCP-powered workflows that move between design, code, and documentation in both directions — design to code, code to design, docs to design system components — using prior decisions as context.
newsArticles.relevance: Open-source signal that MCP-powered design workflows will be platform-agnostic, not just Figma

newsArticles.title: MCP is the USB-C for AI: Design systems as machine-readable intelligence layers
newsArticles.summary: The framing shift of 2026: design systems are no longer just component libraries — they're the intelligence layer AI uses to stay on-brand. DTCG token standards are now the minimum viable export format.
newsArticles.relevance: Fundamental reframe of what a design system is — relevant for VA's VADS evolution strategy

newsArticles.title: How AI + MCP will automate multi-brand design at scale
newsArticles.summary: With Figma's MCP server, a prompt like "update all primary buttons across brands to 16px corner radius" can trigger changes across every brand variant and run visual regression checks automatically.
newsArticles.relevance: Concrete demonstration of how MCP enables design system governance at VA scale

newsArticles.title: Figma MCP server brings Figma context directly into Claude
newsArticles.summary: The Figma MCP connector lets you generate FigJam diagrams, inspect design context, and reference component data from Figma files inside Claude conversations — making Claude a design-aware collaborator.
newsArticles.relevance: Directly actionable for VA designers — the Figma MCP is already available in Claude.ai

newsArticles.title: From prompt engineers to context engineers: MCP in 2026
newsArticles.summary: In 2024 we were prompt engineers. In 2025, RAG architects. In 2026, context engineers are building the infrastructure that connects AI intelligence to real action — and MCP is the substrate.
newsArticles.relevance: Helps VA designers understand what skill to invest in next — context engineering over prompt crafting

newsArticles.title: 2026 predictions: Agentic AI replaces passive chat as the core design pattern
newsArticles.summary: UX researchers now see 2026 as the year "delegative UI" overtakes "conversational UI" — where users assign AI a goal rather than ask it a question. This has major implications for how VA designs AI-powered features.
newsArticles.relevance: Fundamental shift in AI interaction paradigm — affects how VA teams design AI features for Veterans

newsArticles.title: Figma's 2025 AI report: 85% of designers say AI fluency is essential to their future
newsArticles.summary: Despite efficiency gains, fewer than half of designers feel AI makes them better at their jobs. The tension: AI speeds up execution but design judgment — what to make, not how to make it — remains irreplaceably human.
newsArticles.relevance: Evidence-based framing for why VA design teams should invest in AI fluency without losing craft

newsArticles.title: GSA launches FedRAMP 20x to fast-track AI tool authorization for federal agencies
newsArticles.summary: GSA's FedRAMP 20x initiative introduces automated authorization pathways to make it simpler and cheaper for AI cloud providers to achieve federal compliance — with first AI Prioritization authorizations completed in early 2026.
newsArticles.relevance: Directly impacts which AI tools VA contractors can use — FedRAMP authorization is a prerequisite

newsArticles.title: OMB M-25-22: Federal contractors barred from using government data to train AI models
newsArticles.summary: OMB's M-25-22 memorandum requires contracts to prohibit vendors from using non-public government data to train commercial AI algorithms without explicit consent — and mandates clear IP and data portability terms.
newsArticles.relevance: Critical compliance requirement for VA contractors using AI tools — affects tool selection and data handling

newsArticles.title: 2026: Federal agencies move from "AI curiosity" to "AI consequence"
newsArticles.summary: Agencies that spent 2025 in experimentation mode are now implementing targeted, mission-aligned AI solutions. The shift: fewer AI pilots for their own sake, more deployments with repeatable, secure architectures.
newsArticles.relevance: Sets expectations for the environment VA design teams are operating in — AI must show mission outcomes

newsArticles.title: AI democratizes software development across government — "everyone can be a developer"
newsArticles.summary: Mission specialists, policy experts, and administrators are now building applications and automating workflows without traditional programming skills, exponentially expanding government development capacity.
newsArticles.relevance: Has implications for how VA teams think about who builds internal tools — and what skills to develop

newsArticles.title: The AI trust gap: Government's biggest 2026 challenge isn't adoption, it's transparency
newsArticles.summary: As AI tools proliferate in government, the hardest problem is not getting them in the door — it's ensuring transparency, fairness, and public trust in how they're used. Human judgment and accountability remain essential differentiators.
newsArticles.relevance: Directly relevant to VA's AI design principles — trust and transparency aren't just UX concerns, they're institutional ones
